name: Sleep and testosterone optimization

lead: This lifestyle approach tries to raise natural testosterone through sleep, a lean physique, training and diet, often as an alternative to prescription hormones.
Testosterone follows a morning peak and REM sleep is associated with higher night levels, but the sources reviewed contain no human trials of sleep interventions.

paras: Proposed routes are circadian and sleep-related hormone release, less aromatization of testosterone in fat tissue, and training effects. Reference sources describe the body-fat evidence as mixed.
The practices themselves are ordinary lifestyle habits. Concerns raised in sources include assuming low testosterone without testing; diagnosis relies on blood tests, preferably in the morning.

lead: Sleep and testosterone optimization is a lifestyle practice in which men try to raise or protect their natural testosterone through sleep habits, often together with training, leanness and diet. It is popular among people who want to avoid prescription hormone use.

Reference sources note that testosterone follows a daily rhythm, peaking in the morning and falling through the day, and that REM sleep is associated with higher night-time levels [1]. One article reports animal research linking prolonged sleep deprivation to lower testosterone in males [2].

Observational research links low testosterone to insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome in men [3][4]. The sources reviewed did not include trials testing sleep interventions on testosterone in men.

paras: Practitioners combine regular sleep, a lean body, resistance training and a nutritious diet, describing this as a way to raise testosterone naturally. A looksmax.org user asking how to raise testosterone naturally was told the answer was to resume the training and eating habits he had previously followed [5].

Testosterone peaks early each day and falls across the day [1]. Reference sources report REM sleep as associated with higher nocturnal testosterone [1]. Resistance training raises testosterone acutely, endurance training may lower it, and evidence on body fat is mixed, since fat tissue converts testosterone to estradiol but no clear body-mass association has been found [1]. Testosterone is reported to decline about 1 to 3 percent per year in men [6].

Estradiol, produced partly by aromatization of testosterone, is increasingly described as having its own roles in men [7]. Lower testosterone has been associated with insulin resistance in older non-diabetic men independently of measures of central obesity [4].

Testosterone is measured by a blood test, preferably in the morning [6]. An American Urological Association threshold for low testosterone is cited as total testosterone below 300 ng/dL, and screening men without symptoms is not recommended as of 2018 [6].

No studies found. Related research: a cross-sectional study of 2,470 older men reported lower testosterone associated with insulin resistance [4], and a review summarized the association of low testosterone with type 2 diabetes [3]. These observational findings do not test sleep interventions.

lore.intro: Community discussions treat sleep, leanness and training as the foundation of natural testosterone, often as an alternative to Rx options.

claims.claim: Getting back to regular training and clean eating restores testosterone
